headline: Machines boom, payrolls shrink: AI dividend politics reshape a richer, angrier world

events: Two frontier capability jumps in six months: agents reliably complete multi-day software, legal and accounting workflows end to end
Big Tech AI capex passes $900bn annualised; US GDP growth hits 3.2% while hiring of graduates collapses
Fed cuts to 3.0% citing productivity-led disinflation in services; equity indices make record highs
Grid interconnection queues explode; US and Ireland impose data-centre power moratoria in several regions
Ukraine ceasefire along frozen lines; Middle East conflict simmers
Back-office, call-centre and junior professional layoffs accelerate; India and Philippines BPO employment falls ~20%
Electricity prices jump 25-40% in data-centre hubs, pushing G20 inflation to a 4.6% peak; ECB and Fed pause cuts
An autonomous trading/agent cascade freezes a major European card-payments network for 52 hours, triggering EU emergency AI-agent liability rules
US election won on an 'AI dividend' platform: compute and windfall-profit levies promised to fund wage insurance and retraining
China reaches near-frontier open models on domestic chips, keeping tech rivalry intense but trade truces holding
AI-capex digestion: hyperscaler stocks fall 35%, two neo-cloud lenders fail, credit spreads widen; world growth dips to 2.6%
Global unemployment peaks at 7.2%; US unemployment touches 6.8% with white-collar share of jobless at a record
Fed cuts back to 2.5%; US passes Automation Transition Act (wage insurance, payroll-tax cut for human-staffed care work, 2% digital-services/compute levy)
Pakistan, Egypt and Kenya restructure as BPO/remittance income and aid dwindle; Bangladesh garment orders shift to robotic nearshore plants
Mass protests in Manila, Paris and Seoul against 'jobless growth'; a Philippine general strike lasts three weeks
Productivity growth in US services runs ~3.5%/yr; world GDP rebounds to 4.4% on cheaper drugs, software and logistics
AI-designed battery chemistry and grid optimisation speed solar-plus-storage build-out; renewables pass 42% of electricity, but gas and coal are kept on for data-centre baseload
Sovereign stress in Argentina and a smaller Gulf-adjacent issuer; IMF launches an 'automation adjustment' facility
A Sahel-coastal West Africa war and a renewed Israel-Iran exchange count as major new conflicts; AI-guided drones dominate both
Japan's JGB yields spike after BoJ exits YCC fully; MoF defends with automation-driven tax windfalls, averting crisis
Agentic AI used in production by ~63% of firms; cumulative displacement ~215m jobs, partly offset by care, construction, energy and 'human-verified' services
Global unemployment eases to 6.5% but labour share of income hits a modern low; top-1% wealth share jumps
Several EU states pilot universal basic dividends funded by compute and land-value taxes; trust in institutions still sliding
US debt stabilises near 129% of GDP as nominal growth and new levies offset higher transfer spending
Warming reaches ~1.6C; emissions finally decline slightly as AI-optimised grids and EV fleets scale

winners: Hyperscalers, chip designers and owners of power generation/grid assets
High-skill workers who orchestrate AI agents, and skilled trades (electricians, builders, nurses)
US, Taiwan, Gulf states and Nordic countries with cheap power and compute
losers: Mid-career routine white-collar workers and new graduates in rich countries
Services-export economies dependent on BPO and remittances (Philippines, India's IT-services towns, Kenya)
Indebted frontier-market sovereigns facing lost growth models and aid cuts
bullets: The world is measurably richer: global growth averaged ~3.7% and goods and services from software to diagnostics got dramatically cheaper.
Work has been hollowed out in the middle: agents run most back-office, support and junior professional tasks, and the labour share of income is at a modern low.
Politics is organised around 'who owns the machines': compute levies, wage insurance and dividend pilots are spreading but feel too small and too late to most voters.
Electricity is the binding constraint and a cost-of-living flashpoint; data-centre power moratoria and local fights over grid access are routine.
Public debt ratios crept up only modestly because productivity-boosted nominal growth offset transfer spending, but five sovereign restructurings hit the Global South.
Trade blocs held roughly steady: US-China tech rivalry remains fierce, yet tariffs did not escalate and AI services flow across most borders.
Trust in institutions sank further amid AI-driven misinformation, a high-profile agent-caused payments outage, and the sense that gains went to a few firms.
Renewables reached ~45% of power, helped by AI-optimised grids, but surging demand kept fossil plants running and warming hit ~1.6C.
wildcard: In 2028 a cascade of interacting autonomous trading and payment agents froze a major European card network for 52 hours, prompting the first binding AI-agent liability regime.
image_description: In a converted suburban office park outside Manila, former call-centre workers queue for a government retraining stipend while delivery robots glide past and the humming data centre next door glows behind a hand-painted banner reading 'Who Owns the Machines?'
